mainTopic: רבי אליעזר vs. חכמים on one sukkah for seven days and owning your sukkah, plus stories of רבי אליעזר's conduct
overview: This amud opens with a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says you may not switch from one sukkah to another during the חג, and you may not build a new sukkah on חול המועד. חכמים allow both, and everyone agrees that a sukkah that fell down may be rebuilt. The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר reads 'תעשה... שבעת ימים' as 'a sukkah fit for seven days,' while רבנן read it as 'build a sukkah during the חג.' A second ברייתא brings another view of רבי אליעזר: just as you need your own לולב on the first day, you need your own sukkah ('לך'). חכמים answer that 'כל האזרח' shows all of ישראל could sit in one sukkah, so a borrowed sukkah is fine, and each side explains how it reads the other side's פסוק. Next come stories about רבי אליעזר: he praises people who stay home on the רגל, and he avoids answering whether a sheet may be spread over a sukkah because he never said anything he had not heard from his רבי. The גמרא asks how that story fits his own rulings and decides it happened on שבת. It ends by asking why the question was not answered from רבי אליעזר's own ruling about a window shutter, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: No switching sukkahs, no building on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that a person may not move from one sukkah to another during the חג, and may not build a sukkah during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not move from one sukkah to another sukkah, and one may not make a sukkah during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the opinion of רבי אליעזר, who was named just before this amud begins. He gives two strict rules about the sukkah during the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: you must stay in the same sukkah for the whole חג. Rule 2: if you did not build a sukkah before the חג, you cannot build one during חול המועד. Both rules suggest that, in his view, a sukkah must cover all seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: go out / move (here: move from one sukkah to another)
the intermediate days of the Festival (חול המועד)

steps.confusionAlert: Here יוצאין means 'move out' from one sukkah to another. It does NOT mean 'fulfill an obligation' (יוצא ידי חובתו), which shows up later here.

phrases.english: One may not move from one sukkah to another sukkah,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי אליעזר, named in the ברייתא on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and one may not make a sukkah
during the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by continuing the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, there is no switching between sukkahs and no building a sukkah during חול המועד.

steps.title: The Sages permit both
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with both rules: you may switch sukkahs, and you may build a sukkah during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: one may move from one sukkah to another, and one may make a sukkah during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view of חכמים, who reject both of רבי אליעזר's restrictions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the sukkah does not need to last all seven days as one unit. Any kosher sukkah at any point in the חג works.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
One may move from one sukkah to another sukkah,
and one may make a sukkah during the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switching sukkahs and building a sukkah during חול המועד are both allowed.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: a fallen sukkah may be rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that if a sukkah collapses, you may rebuild it during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if it fell down, he rebuilds it during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a point that both sides accept. Even רבי אליעזר allows rebuilding a sukkah that fell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a limit on רבי אליעזר's rule. He forbids building a brand-new sukkah, but he permits restoring the sukkah you already had.

keyTerms.meaning: and they agree (both opinions accept this)
he goes back and rebuilds it

phrases.english: And they agree that if it fell,
he rebuilds it during the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי אליעזר's ban on building during חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rebuilding a collapsed sukkah during חול המועד is permitted according to all opinions.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts analyzing the ברייתא. It asks what source leads רבי אליעזר to his strict view, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for information, not an attack. The גמרא wants the פסוק that drives his opinion.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא to the analysis of the גמרא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי אליעזר's requirement of one sukkah for all seven days.

steps.title: The verse: a sukkah fit for seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'תעשה לך שבעת ימים' as requiring a sukkah built to serve all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Make for yourself חג הסוכות for seven days.' This means: make a sukkah that is fit for seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the פסוק and showing how רבי אליעזר reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'make' and 'seven days' are read together. The act of making must produce a sukkah that lasts seven days. That explains both rules: a sukkah built midway, or a second sukkah you switch to, does not cover seven days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one reading is the root of both of רבי אליעזר's rules in step 1. The same פסוק comes back in step 11, where רבי אליעזר learns a different rule (ownership) from the word 'לך'.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"The Festival of Sukkot you shall make for yourself
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in דברים טז:יג.

phrases.english: seven days,"
make a sukkah that is fit for seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links 'make' with 'seven days,' so the sukkah must be fit for all seven days.

steps.title: How do the Rabbis read that verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבנן deal with this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how חכמים understand the same פסוק, since they do not reach רבי אליעזר's conclusion. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק seems to support רבי אליעזר, רבנן must have another reading of it.

keyTerms.meaning: and the Rabbis? (how do they explain it?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the other side does with the source from step 5.

steps.title: The Rabbis: build a sukkah during the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבנן read the פסוק as allowing you to build the sukkah at any point during the seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the Torah is saying: make a sukkah during the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבנן's reading: 'seven days' describes when you may build, not how long one sukkah must last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, 'seven days' tells you the time window for making the sukkah. So building on חול המועד is actually what the פסוק permits, and switching sukkahs is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what the Torah (lit. the Merciful One) is saying

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק, two readings. רבי אליעזר: one sukkah that lasts seven days. רבנן: you may build the sukkah anytime in the seven days.

phrases.english: This is what the Merciful One is saying:
Make a sukkah during the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Seven days' is the time window for building, so making a sukkah during the חג is allowed.

steps.title: Why say the obvious about a fallen sukkah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the shared ruling about a fallen sukkah and asks why it needs to be stated at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they agree that if it fell, he rebuilds it during חול המועד.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the agreement from step 3 again in order to challenge it. Why would anyone think rebuilding is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuilding your own sukkah seems clearly fine, so the line looks unnecessary. The challenge pushes the גמרא to find the hidden point of the line.

phrases.english: And they agree that if it fell,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחוֹזֵר וּבוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: he rebuilds it during the intermediate days of the Festival.
Is this not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the last line of the ברייתא (step 3) and questions why it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shared ruling that a fallen sukkah may be rebuilt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rebuilding your own sukkah plainly seems permitted, so the ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Without it, we'd think the rebuilt sukkah is a new one
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed so that we do not think a rebuilt sukkah counts as a new sukkah that fails רבי אליעזר's seven-day rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that this is a different sukkah and is not 'for seven days.' So the ברייתא teaches us that it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, according to רבי אליעזר, we might have thought the rebuilt sukkah is a brand-new one. The ברייתא tells us it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר requires a sukkah fit for seven days, and a rebuilt sukkah has not existed for all seven. The ברייתא teaches that it still counts as the original sukkah, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (a mistaken thought)

phrases.english: You might have said
this is a different one
and is not fit for seven days,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא – the line rules out a reasonable mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי אליעזר's seven-day rule, a rebuilt sukkah would count as a new sukkah and be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rebuilt sukkah is still considered the same sukkah, so rebuilding is allowed even according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Setup: you can't use a friend's לולב on the first day
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא of רבי אליעזר begins with a known rule: you cannot use someone else's לולב on the first day, because the פסוק says 'לכם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, just as a person does not fulfill his obligation on the first day of the חג with his friend's לולב, as it says 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms' — meaning from your own...
steps.whatsHappening: This step is the first half of a comparison. It sets up the known לולב rule so that the next step can apply the same idea to sukkah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לכם' (for yourselves) teaches that the לולב must belong to you. This applies on the first day, the day mentioned in the פסוק.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: Just as a person does not fulfill his obligation
on the first festival day of the Festival
with his friend's lulav,
as it is written: "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in ויקרא כג:מ.

phrases.english: the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms" —
from your own,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא with another view of רבי אליעזר, about ownership.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day, one cannot fulfill the מצוה with a borrowed לולב, because of 'לכם.'

steps.title: So too: you can't use a friend's sukkah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר applies the same ownership rule to sukkah, based on 'לך' in 'תעשה לך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ...so too, a person does not fulfill his obligation in his friend's sukkah, as it says 'Make for yourself חג הסוכות for seven days' — meaning from your own.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the comparison. Like the לולב, the sukkah must be your own, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לך' (for yourself) in the sukkah פסוק is read like 'לכם' in the לולב פסוק: it means ownership. This is the same פסוק רבי אליעזר used earlier for 'fit for seven days.' Here he draws a second rule from the word 'לך.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר requires owning your sukkah, just like owning your לולב on day one. He learns it from 'לך' in the same פסוק he used for the seven-day rule.

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: so too, a person does not fulfill his obligation
with his friend's sukkah,
as it is written: "The Festival of Sukkot you shall make for yourself
seven days" —
from your own.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ אֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison set up in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, one does not fulfill the מצוה of sukkah in a friend's sukkah; it must be 'משלך.'

steps.title: The Rabbis allow using a friend's sukkah
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. A friend's לולב does not work on the first day, but a friend's sukkah does work, because 'כל האזרח' teaches that all of ישראל could sit in one sukkah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis say: Even though they said a person cannot fulfill his obligation on the first day of יום טוב with a friend's לולב, he can fulfill his obligation in a friend's sukkah. The פסוק says 'All the homeborn in Israel shall dwell in sukkos.' This teaches that all of ישראל are fit to sit in one sukkah.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side. The חכמים say a friend's sukkah is fine, even though a friend's לולב is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree with the לולב rule from 'לכם' but do not stretch it to sukkah. Their proof is that 'כל האזרח' pictures the entire nation sitting in one sukkah. In that case, no one person could own it, so ownership cannot be required.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the majority view arguing with רבי אליעזר

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are NOT arguing about לולב. They agree that on the first day you need your own לולב. They only argue about sukkah.
steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha follows the חכמים: you may fulfill the מצוה in a borrowed sukkah or a friend's sukkah.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Although they said
a person does not fulfill his obligation

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּלוּלָבוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: on the first day of the Festival with his friend's lulav,
but he does fulfill his obligation
in his friend's sukkah,
as it is written: "All the homeborn in Israel
shall dwell in sukkos,"
this teaches that all of Israel
phrases.notes: If the whole nation shared one sukkah, nobody's share would be worth a פרוטה, so nobody would truly own it.

phrases.english: are fit to sit in one sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר's ownership rule for sukkah in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One fulfills the מצוה of sukkah in a friend's sukkah, based on 'כל האזרח.'

steps.title: What do the Rabbis learn from 'for yourself'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים explain the word 'לך' in 'תעשה לך,' since they do not use it to require ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis, what do they learn from this word 'לך' ('for yourself')?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question. רבי אליעזר used 'לך' to require ownership, so what do the חכמים do with that word?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in the תורה is extra. If the חכמים reject רבי אליעזר's reading of 'לך,' they must have some other use for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they expound from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this word "for yourself,"
what do they expound from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי לְךָ, מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the חכמים to account for the word רבי אליעזר used.

steps.title: 'For yourself' excludes a stolen sukkah
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use 'לך' to exclude a stolen sukkah. A borrowed sukkah is allowed because of 'כל האזרח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to exclude a stolen sukkah. But a borrowed sukkah is allowed, because it is written 'all the homeborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the חכמים, 'לך' means the sukkah cannot be stolen. A borrowed one is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לך' still means 'yours' in a weaker sense. It must be legitimately yours to use, not taken by force. 'כל האזרח' then teaches that a borrowed sukkah counts.

phrases.english: They need it to exclude a stolen sukkah,
but regarding a borrowed one, it is written: "All the homeborn."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לך' excludes a stolen sukkah. A borrowed one is allowed by 'כל האזרח.'

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'all the homeborn'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns it around and asks what רבי אליעזר does with 'כל האזרח,' since he does not use it to allow someone else's sukkah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with this phrase 'all the homeborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about the other side. How does רבי אליעזר use the חכמים' פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has to explain the other side's source. רבי אליעזר does not learn 'one sukkah for everyone' from 'כל האזרח,' so he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, this phrase "all the homeborn,"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי כׇּל הָאֶזְרָח מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 13, now challenging רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from 'כל האזרח.'

steps.title: A גר or a boy who comes of age during סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses 'כל האזרח' to teach that a גר who converts, or a קטן who becomes a גדול, in the middle of סוכות is obligated in sukkah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for a convert who converted in the middle of the festival, and a minor who grew up in the middle of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר uses 'כל האזרח' to include people who become obligated partway through סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to רבי אליעזר's view from earlier steps, that a sukkah must be ready for all seven days. Without this פסוק, we might think someone who was not obligated at the start of the חג never becomes obligated. 'כל' includes them.

keyTerms.meaning: In the meantime, during the festival

phrases.english: He needs it for a convert who converted in the interim
and a minor who came of age in the interim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל האזרח' includes a גר or קטן who becomes obligated during סוכות.

steps.title: Where do the Rabbis learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to the חכמים, who use 'כל האזרח' for something else, how do we know that a mid-festival גר or קטן is obligated?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis? (Where do they learn this law?)
steps.whatsHappening: This one-word question sets up the next answer. The חכמים already used 'כל האזרח,' so where do they get this law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים surely agree that such people are obligated. The question is about their source, since their פסוק is already being used.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis? A short way of asking what the other side holds

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (From where do they learn this?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 16's law back onto the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The חכמים' source for obligating a גר or קטן who becomes obligated mid-festival.

steps.title: No verse is needed for the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים already hold that you may build a sukkah on חול המועד, so obligation can obviously begin mid-festival. No extra פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they said one may build a sukkah during חול המועד, no verse is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים do not need a special פסוק, because their view already allows the מצוה to start in the middle of the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבנן read the פסוק as allowing a sukkah to be built at any time during the seven days. So the מצוה is not tied only to the start of the חג. Someone who becomes obligated later simply starts then. Only רבי אליעזר, who requires a sukkah fit for all seven days, needs a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of the festival

steps.whatToRemember: Each side explains the other's פסוק. For רבנן, 'לך' excludes a stolen sukkah. For רבי אליעזר, 'כל האזרח' includes a mid-festival גר or קטן. רבנן need no פסוק for that, because they allow building a sukkah on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Since they said:
one may make a sukkah during the intermediate days of the festival,
a verse is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ עוֹשִׂין סוּכָּה בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No פסוק is needed, because רבנן already allow building a sukkah on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי visits רבי אליעזר on the רגל
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא tells a story. רבי אלעאי went to greet his rebbi, רבי אליעזר, in לוד on the רגל. רבי אליעזר told him he was not among those who rest at home on the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was an incident with רבי אלעאי, who went to greet his teacher רבי אליעזר in לוד on the festival. רבי אליעזר said to him: אלעאי! You are not among those who rest on the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא with a story about רבי אליעזר. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greeting your rebbi on the רגל is usually a good thing. Here, though, רבי אליעזר criticizes רבי אלעאי for leaving his home. The reason comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who rest (stay home) on the festival

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Elai
who went to greet
Rabbi Eliezer, his teacher, in Lod on the festival.
He said to him: Elai!
You are not among those who rest on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about רבי אליעזר, moving away from the ownership discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר criticized his student for leaving home on the רגל.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר praises those who stay home
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that רבי אליעזר praised even 'lazy' people who stay home on the רגל, because the פסוק says 'ושמחת אתה וביתך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אליעזר used to say: I praise the lazy people, who do not leave their homes on the festival, as it is written: 'And you shall rejoice, you and your household.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's criticism. One should be home on the רגל, rejoicing with one's household.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וביתך' ('your household') is understood to mean one's wife. You cannot rejoice with her if you are away from home. So even a 'lazy' person who stays home is doing the מצוה, and someone who travels away is missing it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall rejoice, you and your household'

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not praising laziness itself. He is praising people who stay home, even if they do it only out of laziness, because staying home fulfills שמחת יום טוב with one's family.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Eliezer used to say:
I praise the lazy ones,
who do not leave their homes on the festival,
as it is written: "And you shall rejoice, you and your household."
phrases.notes: 'Your household' is understood to mean one's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי אֶת הָעַצְלָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי אליעזר's remark in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that one should stay home on the רגל.

steps.title: But we must go greet our teacher on the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's praise of people who stay home. It uses רבי יצחק's teaching that a person is obligated to greet his רבי on the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really true? רבי יצחק said: How do we know a person must go greet his teacher on the festival? Because the פסוק says, 'Why are you going to him today? It is neither חודש nor שבת.' This implies that on חודש and שבת a person is obligated to greet his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous step. רבי אליעזר praised people who stay home on the רגל, but רבי יצחק says you must go out to greet your רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the husband of the שונמית asks why she is going to the נביא on a day that is not חודש or שבת. That means people normally did go to their רבי on such days. So going out to greet your רבי seems to be required, and staying home seems to be the wrong thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This opens a challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak say:
From where do we know that one is obligated to greet
his teacher on the festival?
As it says: "Why are you going to him today?
phrases.notes: This is from מלכים ב ד:כג, where the husband of the שונמית is speaking to his wife.

phrases.english: It is neither the New Moon nor Shabbat."
This implies that on the New Moon and Shabbat
a person is obligated to greet his teacher!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the praise of staying home in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's praise of people who stay home on the רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק derives from a פסוק that one must go out to greet his רבי on the רגל, which seems to contradict staying home.

steps.title: Same-day trip versus overnight trip
steps.stepSummary: Going to one's רבי is required when he can return home the same day. Staying home is praised when the trip would keep him away overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. רבי יצחק is talking about someone who goes and comes back the same day. רבי אליעזר is talking about someone who goes and cannot come back the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each statement applies to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person can come back the same day, he can still celebrate with his family at night, so he should go greet his רבי. If the trip would keep him away overnight, he would miss the family שמחה of 'ושמחת אתה וביתך,' so staying home is better.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; this opens an answer.
Goes and returns on the same day

steps.whatToRemember: Greeting your רבי on the רגל is required only when you can return home the same day. Otherwise, staying home to rejoice with your family comes first.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one refers to where he goes and returns on the same day,
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבי יצחק's obligation applies.

phrases.english: and that one refers to where he goes and does not return on the same day.
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבי אליעזר praises staying home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going to one's רבי and staying home seemed to be opposite rules for the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: A same-day trip is required. A trip that keeps him away overnight is not, and staying home is praised.

steps.title: The story begins: the sun shines into the sukkah
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets the scene. רבי אליעזר was staying in the סוכה of יוחנן בן רבי אלעאי, and the sun began shining into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Once רבי אליעזר stayed in the Upper גליל, in the סוכה of יוחנן son of רבי אלעאי in קיסרי (some say קיסריון). The sun reached the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This line only sets up the scene for the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun coming through the סכך made the סוכה uncomfortable. That creates the practical problem: may they cover it with a sheet?

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer
who stayed in the Upper Galilee
in the sukkah of Yochanan son of Rabbi Elai
in Caesarea, and some say in Caesarion,
and the sun reached the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scene-setting: רבי אליעזר was a guest in another person's סוכה, and the sun was shining in.

steps.title: May I spread a sheet over it?
steps.stepSummary: יוחנן asks רבי אליעזר whether he may spread a sheet over the סוכה to block the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May I spread a sheet over it?
steps.whatsHappening: יוחנן asks a practical הלכה question: is it permitted to cover the סוכה with a sheet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is whether adding a cover is allowed, since it may count as making a temporary tent (אהל עראי). The story seems to take place on a festival, but the גמרא later concludes it happened on שבת. This is a real halachic question, and it needs an answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the law, may I spread
a sheet over it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מַהוּ שֶׁאֶפְרוֹשׂ עָלֶיהָ סָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question that the scene in step 23 created.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may spread a sheet over the סוכה to block the sun

steps.title: An unrelated answer about judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not answer directly. Instead he says that every שבט produced a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no tribe in ישראל that did not produce a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר replies with a statement that has nothing to do with the question. He is avoiding giving a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say yes or no about the sheet. Step 29 explains why he answered this way.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to find a hidden ruling about the sheet in this answer. רבי אליעזר is deliberately changing the subject, and step 29 explains why.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט
phrases.english: He said to him: There is no tribe
of Israel that did not produce a judge from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to the question in step 24 without giving a ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling. He gives an unrelated statement about judges from every שבט.

steps.title: The sun spreads, and the question is asked again
steps.stepSummary: Now the sun covers half the סוכה, and יוחנן asks again whether he may spread a sheet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sun reached half the סוכה. He said to him: May I spread a sheet over it?
steps.whatsHappening: The problem gets worse, so יוחנן repeats the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same as before, but now it is more urgent because the sun is shining on more of the סוכה.

phrases.english: The sun reached half of the sukkah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מַהוּ שֶׁאֶפְרוֹשׂ עָלֶיהָ סָדִין?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the law, may I spread a sheet over it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question from step 24 because the problem has grown.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Again, whether a sheet may be spread over the סוכה

steps.title: Another unrelated answer about prophets and kings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר again avoids a ruling. He says every שבט produced נביאים, and that יהודה and בנימין had kings appointed by נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no tribe in ישראל that did not produce prophets. The tribes of יהודה and בנימין appointed kings according to the word of prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: Once again, רבי אליעזר answers with something unrelated instead of ruling on the sheet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move as step 25. The kings he refers to are שאול from בנימין and דוד from יהודה, who were anointed by שמואל הנביא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט
phrases.english: He said to him: There is no tribe
of Israel from which prophets did not come out.
The tribes of Judah and Benjamin
appointed kings according to prophets.
phrases.notes: שאול and דוד were anointed by שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יָצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ נְבִיאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to the repeated question in step 26, again without giving a ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling. He gives an unrelated statement about prophets and kings.

steps.title: יוחנן spreads the sheet and רבי אליעזר leaves
steps.stepSummary: When the sun reaches רבי אליעזר's feet, יוחנן spreads the sheet himself, and רבי אליעזר walks out of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sun reached רבי אליעזר's feet. יוחנן took a sheet and spread it over the סוכה. רבי אליעזר threw his cloak over his shoulder behind him and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its climax. יוחנן acts on his own, and רבי אליעזר shows by leaving that he does not approve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר never said it was forbidden, but he would not stay under a sheet that had not been permitted to him. His action says what his words did not.

keyTerms.meaning: He threw it over his shoulder

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ חַמָּה לְמַרְגְּלוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: The sun reached the feet of Rabbi Eliezer.
Yochanan took a sheet and spread it over it.

phrases.aramaic: הִפְשִׁיל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר טַלִּיתוֹ לַאֲחוֹרָיו וְיָצָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer threw his cloak behind him and went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ חַמָּה לְמַרְגְּלוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story after the two evasive answers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר left rather than sit under a sheet that had not been permitted.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר avoided answering
steps.stepSummary: The text then explains that רבי אליעזר was not brushing יוחנן off. He simply never said anything he had not heard from his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not because he was trying to push him off with words. It was because he never said anything that he had not heard from his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains the strange answers. רבי אליעזר had no tradition from his רבי about the sheet, so he would not rule on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His unrelated answers were not rude. They came from a strict principle: rule only on what you received from your teacher. Since he had no received ruling, he did not give one.

keyTerms.meaning: From the mouth of his teacher

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר never said a ruling he had not heard from his רבי. That is why he changed the subject instead of answering.

phrases.english: Not because he was diverting him with words,
but because he never said a thing
that he did not hear from the mouth of his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the evasive answers in steps 25 and 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר only taught what he had received from his רבי.

steps.title: How could he be a guest in another sukkah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר could stay in someone else's סוכה, since he himself holds that you may not go from one סוכה to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do that? Didn't רבי אליעזר say that one may not go out from one סוכה to another סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story using רבי אליעזר's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person must stay in one סוכה for the whole חג. Yet here he is staying in יוחנן's סוכה, away from his own. That seems to contradict his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not move from one sukkah to another

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
One may not go out from one sukkah to another sukkah!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the setting of the story told in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's staying in יוחנן's סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own ruling forbids moving from one סוכה to another, yet he was a guest in someone else's סוכה.

steps.title: It happened on a different festival
steps.stepSummary: The story took place on a different רגל, not סוכות, so the rule about סוכה does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a different festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story did not happen on סוכות, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They were sitting in the סוכה only to enjoy the shade and fresh air, not to fulfill the מצוה. So רבי אליעזר's rule against moving from one סוכה to another does not apply. The sheet question was then about adding a covering on יום טוב, not about the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the story uses the word 'סוכה,' it was not סוכות. The booth was used only as a shady place on another יום טוב.

phrases.english: It was a different festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the setting of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the story happened on סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It happened on another רגל, so the rule about moving between סוכות does not apply.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר praises people who stay home on the Festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer that the story was on another רגל. רבי אליעזר praised people who do not leave home on a רגל, so he would not have been a guest away from home then.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אליעזר say: I praise the 'lazy' people who do not leave their homes on the רגל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer, that the story happened on a different רגל. It quotes רבי אליעזר himself saying it is praiseworthy to stay home on a רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31 the גמרא moved the story to another יום טוב to avoid the problem of switching סוכות. But if רבי אליעזר thinks people should stay home on every רגל, it makes no sense that he was away from home staying with יוחנן. So the 'different רגל' answer clashes with his own teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say…? (opens a challenge from a known statement)
'Lazy' people, here meaning those who stay home
On the Festival (one of the three pilgrimage holidays)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lazy' here is not an insult. רבי אליעזר is praising people who stay home on יום טוב to celebrate with their families. He calls them 'lazy' only because they do not go out.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
I praise the lazy ones
who do not leave their houses on the Festival!
phrases.notes: This covers every רגל, not only סוכות, so the answer in step 31 does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 31 (that the story was on a different רגל).
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the story took place on a רגל other than סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר praises people who stay home on a רגל. So he would not have been a guest in someone else's home on any רגל.

steps.title: It was שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the story happened on a regular שבת, not on a יום טוב at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the story took place on שבת, not on a רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's praise for staying home applies to a רגל, not to an ordinary שבת. So his being a guest on שבת does not contradict his teaching. This also means יוחנן's earlier question about spreading a sheet was really about building on שבת.

phrases.english: It was Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Now the sheet question is about the מלאכה of building on שבת, not about סוכה rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the setting of the story (שבת instead of יום טוב).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the story was on some רגל, which clashes with רבי אליעזר's praise of staying home on a רגל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story was on an ordinary שבת, not a רגל. The praise of staying home does not apply, and the sheet question was about building on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's own ruling on a window shutter should answer the question
steps.stepSummary: If the question was about building on שבת, יוחנן could have learned the answer from רבי אליעזר's own ruling in the משנה about plugging a window on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him figure out the answer from רבי אליעזר's own words, as we learned in a משנה: about a window shutter, רבי אליעזר says that when it is tied and hanging, one may shutter the window with it, and if not, one may not. The חכמים say that either way one may shutter with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the 'it was שבת' answer. If the question was about building on שבת, רבי אליעזר already ruled on a similar case in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר forbids using a shutter to close a window on שבת unless it is already tied and hanging there, because otherwise it counts like adding to a structure. Spreading a sheet on a סוכה is also adding to a temporary tent. So רבי אליעזר's own view seems to forbid it, and יוחנן should not have needed to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Then resolve it for him (why is this still a question?)
Tied and hanging (already attached to the window)
One may plug or shutter (the window)

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא is assuming that, according to רבי אליעזר, adding to a temporary covering on שבת can count as building. That is the real halachic question behind יוחנן's request about the sheet. The גמרא's response to this challenge comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Then resolve it for him from his own view,
as we learned in a mishna: a window shutter,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
when it is tied and hanging (from the window)
one may shutter the window with it,
phrases.notes: Since it is already attached, closing the window does not count as building.

phrases.english: and if not, one may not shutter with it.
And the Rabbis say:
In both cases one may shutter with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty that comes from the answer in step 33 (it was שבת).
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that יוחנן's question about spreading the sheet on שבת was an open question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר already forbids closing a window with an unattached shutter on שבת because it counts as adding to a structure. Spreading a sheet on a סוכה is the same kind of adding, so his own ruling seems to answer the question, and he should not have avoided giving an answer.
